AFRICAM 27AC.summary: Students describe highly engaging, passionate lectures and a fairly easy class if you keep up with the readings. Reading is long but interesting. Grades depend largely on the section instructor, and attendance can be mandatory with no recordings. Reviewers strongly recommend it.

AFRICAM 5A.summary: Students describe engaging lectures, a reading-heavy but manageable class, and a light workload with a few take-home assignments. Discussion attendance is mandatory. The most repeated complaint is very slow, sometimes unclear grading, so grades may not appear before the P/NP deadline.

AGRS 28.summary: Students say lectures are dense and info-heavy, slides are sparse, and recordings are often not available. Reading load and quizzes are heavy, and several say the workload is too much for a breadth course. A few found the material interesting and the lectures captivating. Reviews lean negative.

AGRS R44.summary: Students say lectures are funny and engaging for many, though some find them dry. The class has heavy reading, three essays and a final, and your grade depends largely on your GSI. Reviewers advise keeping up with readings and note it suits those interested in classics.

AMERSTD 10.summary: Reviews are mixed. Some enjoy the engaging, witty lectures and nuanced perspectives, while others find them boring or find the instructor dismissive of disagreement. Expect three papers, a midterm, a final, graded attendance, and no posted slides. Grading is described as harsh for an intro class.

ANTHRO 1.summary: Students describe a fairly easy class with weekly quizzes, a midterm and a final, with questions drawn from lecture slides. Lectures are often called dense or boring, but slides are posted. Steady studying and keeping up with the lab book and quizzes are the main advice.

ANTHRO 107.summary: Reviewers find the material fascinating and the lectures enthusiastic, with approachable staff. Opinions on difficulty differ: one calls it very easy, others say exams are tough and hard to predict because they can cover any slide. Do not rely on lecture recordings, which had audio problems.

ANTHRO 114.summary: Few reviews. The readings and lectures are dense and hard, and several older reviews found lectures difficult to understand. A recent review found the material well explained and rewarding. The course focuses on the history of social and cultural anthropology.

ANTHRO 157.summary: Reviews are polarized. Some call it a favorite, with inspiring lectures built on personal anecdotes and current events that reward close attention. Others find tangents hard to follow and the reading excessive. Grading is by in-class written exams weighted toward the final.

ANTHRO 189.summary: Reviews are mixed. Some enjoy the engaging, discussion-based classes with weekly readings and posts, a generous grade and unclear criteria. Others found lectures dull or off topic, readings dense, and seminar discussions poorly organized. It is described as an easy A by some.

ANTHRO 2AC.summary: Most reviewers are negative, citing mandatory attendance, a no-electronics rule, graded in-class notecards, heavy reading, and unpredictable, very specific quizzes. Lectures are called disorganized and boring. A few say it was an easy A with extra credit and that most reading is unnecessary, but most advise taking another breadth class.

ANTHRO 3AC.summary: Students describe a reading-heavy class with dry or digressive lectures and a few essays or a final project. Many say it is an easy A if you keep up, and that discussion sections and teaching assistants carry the learning. Some find grading subjective and exam prompts hard.

ANTHRO C12AC.summary: Students call it an easy, enjoyable American Cultures course with engaging lectures and guest speakers. It involves readings discussed in discussion sections, a couple of exams and one research paper. Grading is generous, though content can feel repetitive.

ARCH 100B.summary: Students overwhelmingly praise the studio for supportive, inspiring feedback and instructors who stay late to review projects. Reviewers say effort and time commitment are expected. One very old review described the studio as disorganized.

ARCH 100C.summary: Reviewers are very positive about a creative, encouraging studio that rewards effort and gives good feedback. Sessions often run over time, and students get out of it what they put in. It is described as one of the more enjoyable design studios.

ASAMST 121.summary: Students say the instructor is kind and knowledgeable, but the class is loosely structured and lectures can be dry. Workload includes weekly writing, a group project and some quizzes on specific facts. Reviewers call it manageable and easy to do well in, best for those interested in the topic.

ASAMST 20AC.summary: Students describe a relaxed class with low homework, weekly readings, and quizzes that allow multiple attempts, plus extra credit. Warnings: the midterm and final are closed-book, timed multiple choice with specific factual questions, so it is not as easy an A as rumored. Discussion attendance is mandatory.

ASAMST W20AC.summary: Students describe a manageable, mostly online class with recorded lectures, weekly quizzes with multiple attempts and a group podcast project. Readings are extensive and quizzes and exams can ask for small details. Lectures are seen as interesting but monotone, and GSIs matter.

ASTRON C10.summary: Reviewers find the lectures engaging and the topics fascinating, but say the class is harder than a typical breadth. Expect weekly homework, labs, quizzes and a tough, tricky final, though the curve is generous. Many advise taking it Pass/No Pass unless you like STEM.

BIOENG 100.summary: Opinions split. Many describe an easy, lenient ethics course with manageable homework, a debate and a take-home final, and some mention no exams. Others report unclear rubrics, mistakes in materials and an unenthusiastic lecture style. Showing up and doing the homework is said to be enough.

BIOLOGY 1A.summary: Reviewers describe an exam-heavy class with difficult, uncurved exams and lectures that many find disorganized or too dense. The genetics unit is called the hardest. Students say you must teach yourself from the textbook and recorded lectures, and attendance is enforced.

BIOLOGY 1AL.summary: Students call this a busy, dense lab course with manageable labs but exams that many consider very hard, with little partial credit. Lectures are mostly liked and effectively required because of pre-lab rules. Opinions split on fairness, and several say it is not an easy A.

BIOLOGY 1B.summary: Students say the course is split into three units taught by different instructors, and quality and difficulty vary by unit. The plant and organism unit is dense and fast, while ecology is seen as easier and well organized. Reviewers advise rewatching recordings, using handouts and making flashcards.

BUDDSTD C50.summary: Students call this a challenging but transformative course with engaging lectures, but expect heavy reading, weekly short essays that are graded strictly, weekly quizzes and mandatory attendance. Section instructors strongly affect grades, and extra credit helps. It rewards commitment.

CHEM 12A.summary: Students say this is a hard, time-heavy organic chemistry course with frequent assignments. Most praise clear, organized lectures with in-class practice, fair grading and helpful office hours. A few found the workload excessive and the mechanism explanations vague. Lots of practice is the common advice.

CHEM 135.summary: Reviewers say the material is hard and memorization-heavy, including drawing many mechanisms. Lectures are described as organized and clear, with practice problems and extra credit that help. Opinions differ on exams: some call them fair, others say grading is unclear and questions unpredictable.

CHEM 1A.summary: Students describe a standard first-semester chemistry course with fairly challenging tests, easy-to-earn discussion credit, and plenty of practice exams. Lectures are widely praised as engaging, though a few say acids and bases are hard and some instructors confuse. Reviewers advise doing practice tests and going to office hours.

CHEM 1AL.summary: Students say the labs are straightforward, but weekly pre-labs and lab reports take far more time than a 2-unit class suggests. Grading is described as strict and unclear, with no rubric and big differences between GSIs. Lectures are fun but often unrelated to the labs, and the final closely mirrors the practice exams.

CHEM 1B.summary: Reviews are mixed. Students say exams are manageable if you do the practice exams, and some appreciate free materials and helpful office hours. Others complain of heavy work, online homework that does not match lectures, errors in practice solutions, and topics on exams not covered.

CHEM 32.summary: Students describe an easy, well-structured prep course with caring teaching and very accessible office hours. Exams are fair and homework is harder than the tests. Many say it built a solid foundation for later chemistry, and it is often taken pass/no pass.

CHEM 3A.summary: Students call this organic chemistry course demanding, with fast lectures, frequent assignments and quizzes, and a lot of work. Many say staying on top of the material, practicing, and attending office hours leads to success, and several note generous drops and cheat sheets. Opinions on teaching quality vary widely by instructor.

CHEM 3AL.summary: Students describe a manageable, well-organized lab course with clear grading, helpful lectures tied to the labs, and a responsive instructor. Common warnings are that the final is harder than the practice exams and that notebook and lab report grading can be picky. Showing up and doing the work is enough for most.

CHEM 3B.summary: Students say organic chemistry is hard and the workload is heavy, but most find the lectures clear and the grading fair. Extra credit, dropped scores, notes on exams and office hours help. Reviewers urge doing all practice problems and going to office hours, though a few found the style hard to fit.

CHEM 3BL.summary: Students generally like the lectures and find exams fair, and many praise how approachable the instructor is. Grading on data analysis and lab assignments is described as strict, with small mistakes costing many points. Expect several assignments each week, and go to office hours for help.

CHEM 4A.summary: Students say lectures are engaging but dense, and exams are the hard part, with unclear question types and little exam prep. Grading is seen as fair by some and harsh by others. Reviewers advise reading the textbook, using GSI resources, and going to office hours. A midterm drop is mentioned.

CHEM 4B.summary: Students say this is a demanding course in a notoriously hard series, with tough exams and a heavy lab load. Opinions on lectures split, from engaging and fair to flat and confusing. Reviewers mention that practice exams do not match the real ones and that the head GSI matters a lot.

CHEM C182.summary: Reviewers largely love this class, praising an enthusiastic, clear instructor, clear expectations, helpful office hours and interesting content such as field trips. One review found the concepts poorly explained and demos unhelpful for the midterm. Overall students strongly recommend it.

CHMENG 140.summary: Students call this a very difficult, fast-paced course with long problem sets and tough exams, but most praise the teaching and say it is rewarding. Going to every lecture, discussion, and office hours is repeatedly advised, and working with others on homework helps. Some find lectures disorganized or intimidating.

CIVENG 60.summary: Reviewers agree the exams are easy, with cheat sheets allowed and test content previewed, so an A is very achievable. However, most say lectures are disorganized and poor, and you will learn little from them. Homework and labs clarify what you need to know.

CIVENG 93.summary: Students rate this very highly for organized, clear lectures, fair grading, and approachable teaching. It is a demanding class with lots of homework, quizzes, labs, a project, and long, difficult exams, but partial credit is generous. Reviewers say attending lecture, studying, and using office hours pays off.

CIVENG C30.summary: Reviewers describe an easy to moderate class with some boring or hard-to-follow lectures and a decent amount of homework. Exams are close to practice problems and the instructor hints at what is covered, though one student found the final differed. Attending lecture for hints and doing the homework are recommended.

COGSCI 1.summary: Reviewers mostly find it an easy, entertaining intro with a generous curve and plenty of extra credit. Exams are multiple choice from the slides, and iClicker attendance matters. Lectures are fast and slide-heavy, the 3 hour option drags, and some dislike the teaching style.

COGSCI 115.summary: Students find the topic interesting and often life-improving, with entertaining lectures. Common complaints: attendance clicker points are a big part of the grade, exams demand memorizing many detailed slides, and assignment instructions are vague. Exams are curved and described as tough but doable with heavy studying.

COGSCI 180.summary: Students generally enjoy this philosophical, personally meaningful class and call the lectures warm and engaging. Exams can be tricky and memorization-based, but a generous curve and extra credit make an A manageable. Clicker attendance counts, and there are two papers.

COGSCI 190.summary: Students mostly enjoyed this happiness and neuroscience topics course, citing interesting research, practical exercises and curved exams. Some find the content life changing, while one reviewer found lectures slide-reading with subjective grading. Expect to learn brain structures and study the slides.

COGSCI C100.summary: Reviewers like the engaging stories and interesting topics, and note lenient grading and curved exams. Frequent iClicker quizzes count heavily, so attendance matters. Critics call it shallow, memorization-based, with a big group project and unclear grading.

COGSCI N100.summary: Reviews are split. Many love the engaging, story-filled lectures on practical topics like memory and mindfulness, while others find the daily quizzes, nitpicky exams, long lectures and group work frustrating. Quizzes count heavily and attendance matters.

COLWRIT R1A.summary: Reviews are divided. Many describe a heavy, time-consuming writing workload with harsh grading and repeated revisions, plus some complaints about vague expectations. Others say the detailed feedback and revisions made them better writers. Experience seems to vary a lot by instructor.

COLWRIT R4A.summary: Reviews are mostly negative and depend on the instructor. Students describe vague prompts, strict or inconsistent grading, discouraging feedback, and heavy workload with frequent office hours needed. A few say the class is supportive with chances to revise, and that effort and participation pay off.

COLWRIT R4B.summary: Students describe a very demanding writing course with heavy workload, many assignments, and harsh grading. Some value the detailed feedback and freedom to choose research topics, while many report an unsupportive, inflexible environment and say they would take a different section. Reviews are sharply divided and lean negative.

COMLIT 60AC.summary: Students describe a warm, low-stress class with manageable reading, group work and a few essays or a final project. There are no major exams. Reviewers say the instructor is caring and accommodating, and that it is a good way to satisfy the American Cultures requirement.

COMLIT W60AC.summary: Students describe a warm, supportive class with manageable reading, flexible essay topics and a group creative project. There are no final exams in most accounts, and deadlines or reading loads are often eased. Attendance and group work are expected.

COMPSCI 10.summary: Reviewers praise the engaging lectures, welcoming approach, and generous retake and clobber policies, calling it a good intro for beginners. Others say the labs are long, exams and the postterm are very difficult, and some found the teaching hard to follow. Falling behind is hard to recover from, especially in summer.

COMPSCI 161.summary: Students find the security course interesting and enjoyable, with engaging lectures and fun but sometimes annoying projects. Exams and one big project count for much of the grade. Reviewers mention flexible extensions and generous curving.

COMPSCI 170.summary: Students find the content challenging but interesting and useful for problem solving, though not essential unless you like theory. Homework resembles CS 70. Lecture quality varies a lot by instructor, and reviewers recommend discussions and the textbook.

COMPSCI 188.summary: Reviewers are overwhelmingly positive about the lectures, describing them as clear, supportive and humane, with flexible policies. One reviewer disliked the course content itself, and one older review was strongly negative. Lectures help a lot with the probability half.

COMPSCI 189.summary: Reviewers are very positive about the teaching, citing clear intuition, good lecture notes and flexible deadlines. Exams are described as hard but fair, and homework is heavy for some. One reviewer calls the workload excessive, and the Spring offering is said to be less math heavy than Fall.

COMPSCI 61A.summary: Students say the class is fast-paced and exam-driven, with heavy emphasis on recursion. It is much easier with prior programming experience and very hard without it. Recent reviews complain about a very hard final, strict grading and a low average, while praising lectures. Practice exams and homework are the advice given.

COMPSCI 61B.summary: Students call it a fun, useful data structures class with interesting projects and clear, engaging lectures. Workload is heavy and exams are described as difficult but fair. Reviewers advise using office hours, since it is hard to learn without guidance.

COMPSCI 61C.summary: Students find the material interesting and lectures engaging, with long, time-consuming projects and hard exams. Many warn that grading in recent semesters was stressful, with low exam averages and bins that did not shift. Reviewers recommend it if you care about learning more than GPA.

COMPSCI 70.summary: Students describe a fast, challenging course where exams are very hard and lectures often follow slides with little explanation. Most say learning happens through reading the notes beforehand, discussions, homework and outside videos. A few find the instructor caring and the material rewarding.

COMPSCI C182.summary: Students praise the lectures as clear and insightful for understanding deep learning, and say the course is demanding with a heavy workload. Complaints include disorganized logistics, unclear grading, uneven TA quality, and exams or extra credit that felt disconnected. Teaching style is polarizing, though many say it was worth it.

DATA 94.summary: Students strongly recommend this ethics and technology course with engaging lectures and interesting readings, not coding-based. Workload is low, with a short essay midterm with questions given in advance, a presentation and a final essay. Attendance is mandatory. Some wish for more data science focus.

DATA C140.summary: Students praise engaging, clear lectures and an excellent textbook. They describe the course as challenging, with heavy, tough homework and a large time commitment that pays off. Reviewers advise attending lecture, keeping up and following instructions closely. Exams are called fair.

DATA C8.summary: Students call it an approachable intro to stats and coding, especially for those with no background, with engaging lectures. Homework and labs are manageable, but many say exams are tougher or trickier than expected. Reviewers advise attending labs and sections and practicing past exams.

DATA C88C.summary: Students call it a useful but uneven course, a lighter version of CS 61A with weekly homework and labs. Reviews disagree on difficulty: easy with prior coding experience, hard without it. Strong support and resources are noted, and deadlines matter.

DESINV 181.summary: Students describe an engaging, practical design course with thoughtful feedback and useful industry insight. It needs no design background, and three projects in one term move quickly. Reviewers say the instructor is approachable and supportive.

DESINV 21.summary: Reviewers overwhelmingly call this one of their favorite and most useful classes, praising clear teaching and honest feedback. Assignments and projects are time-consuming but worthwhile, and work can be redone for a better grade. Students say it builds practical skills and a portfolio, and the waitlist is often full.

DUTCH 161AC.summary: Students describe an easy, low-workload, interesting class with one short weekly writing assignment, a few bigger essays, and light participation. Attendance is relaxed, lectures are not recorded but slides are shared, and grading is straightforward. Reviewers recommend it, though lectures can be hard to hear.

DUTCH 166.summary: Reviewers largely love this history course, citing interesting lectures, a friendly and accommodating style, easy open-note exams and manageable coursework. Showing up and participating is said to lead to a good grade. A couple of older reviews found it dull and unhelpful about grades.

DUTCH 171AC.summary: Students describe an easy, enjoyable American Cultures course with storytelling lectures and a caring instructor. Work is mostly short weekly assignments, participation, and open-note essay exams. Regular attendance and participation are advised for a high grade, and the accent can be hard to follow.

DUTCH C178.summary: Reviewers are uniformly positive, describing an engaging, discussion-friendly course with a kind instructor and interesting readings. Exams were open note in at least one semester. Students recommend attending lecture.

ECON 1.summary: Reviewers mostly love the lectures and say the course pack is the key to doing well on exams. Several note exams can include topics not covered in lecture, and some find lectures unhelpful for tests. Expect a few midterms and an essay final; most call it fair and manageable.

ECON 100A.summary: Students say lectures are engaging and a detailed course pack closely matches exams, so doing its problems is the key advice. Midterms can be hard and time-pressured, there are three with the lowest dropped, and the final is an essay. Some find the structure loose.

ECON 100B.summary: Reviewers mostly describe boring or unclear lectures, with sections doing most of the teaching. Exams are hard and calculus-heavy, problem sets use Excel, and grading is slow and strict. Students advise relying on sections and problem sets and studying a lot.

ECON 101A.summary: Reviewers say this is a very challenging, math-heavy course with fast, content-packed lectures and exam averages around 30 percent, offset by a curve. Practice worksheets and problem sets help. Opinions split between those who value the rigor and those who say lectures do not prepare students for exams.

ECON 119.summary: Reviewers find the lectures engaging and the topic interesting. Opinions split on difficulty, with some calling problem sets and exams fair and others finding problem sets long, hard and weakly tied to exams. Attendance is mandatory and electronics are not allowed.

ECON 136.summary: Reviewers are strongly negative, describing a test-only grade of two midterms and a final, dry lectures, heavy self-study and a harsh curve. Exams reportedly follow the problem sets and practice problems, so working those helps. Strong math skills and memorization are needed.

ECON 139.summary: Reviewers are largely negative. They say the course offers no slides, recordings, GSIs or sections, only student-written notes with errors, and very hard exams that differ from lecture. Heavy self-study is needed, though the curve is described as generous.

ECON 140.summary: Reviewers say the course is dry, math-heavy and proof-focused, with lectures that many find hard to follow. Grading is often described as unclear, though some find the class fair if you do practice exams and attend sections. Opinions are split, with several saying its bad reputation is exaggerated.

ECON 141.summary: Reviewers are mostly negative about teaching, describing proof-heavy, hard-to-follow lectures with tangents and little exam preparation. Exams are difficult and curve and grading criteria are said to be unclear. Problem sets, lecture slides and section help are the main resources. Self-study is needed.

ECON 2.summary: Students agree the class is test-heavy, with grades driven mainly by a midterm and final. Slides and recordings are not posted, so attendance matters, and exams may draw on readings and small lecture details. Opinions split: some find it manageable if you attend and do practice problems, others find it unfair.

ECON C110.summary: Students say game theory is taught with fun in-class games and engaging lectures, though the course is more mathematical than expected. Exams and problem sets are challenging, and some find explanations unclear and support limited. Reviewers advise doing the problem sets and attending lecture.

ECON N110.summary: Students say game theory is taught with fun in-class games and engaging lectures, though the course is more mathematical than expected. Exams and problem sets are challenging, and some find explanations unclear and support limited. Reviewers advise doing the problem sets and attending lecture.

EECS 127.summary: Students say lectures are clear and the course is a solid foundation for machine learning, with challenging homework. Exams are described as fair if you do the homework. Several recent reviews object to a grading scheme where the final counts for most of the grade and homework counts for nothing.

ELENG 120.summary: Students say the course is theory-heavy and about average for upper-division difficulty, with long homework and sometimes time-pressured exams. Most reviews praise clear, funny lectures and helpful office hours. Attending lectures and doing homework carefully is the repeated advice.

ELENG 16A.summary: Students describe a challenging, linear-algebra-focused course with hard homework and labs, and some disorganization after recent curriculum changes. Lectures are engaging for many, though some find them hard to follow. Exams are open book but difficult and time-pressured. Reviewers say discussion and homework are key.

ELENG 16B.summary: Reviewers are mostly negative, describing a stressful, disorganized course with difficult exams, harsh policies, and little or no clobber or curve. Lectures are often called slow or not helpful, and labs are hard without prior circuits experience. A few say the final was fair and that prior EE experience helps greatly.

ENGIN 125.summary: Students say the content is easy and an A is attainable, but the course is widely described as disorganized, with confusing assignments, shifting deadlines and strict attendance and device rules. It satisfies ethics and H/SS requirements. Most reviewers would not recommend it unless needed.

ENGIN 128.summary: Reviews are limited and mixed. Homework is manageable until the animation section, and the final animation project is a huge time sink toward the end. Lab attendance is a must. Some praise the class and project, while others say explanations are weak but grading is lenient.

ENGIN 25.summary: Students say the workload is far beyond what a 2-unit class suggests, with long drafting assignments and hard exams graded by tough GSIs. Lectures are seen as dull or not very useful, and solutions are rarely provided. Some note a curve and fair help at lab. Reviews are mostly negative.

ENGIN 26.summary: Students describe an easy introduction to CAD where nearly all learning happens in labs with the GSI, while lectures are online, boring and mainly useful for the participation quiz. The final group project and report are graded arbitrarily, so reviewers advise being careful there. Prior CAD experience makes it a breeze.

ENGIN 27.summary: Reviewers are strongly negative, reporting confusing lectures, busy work, unclear and slow grading, and a workload heavy for a 2-unit course. Participation is required even though lectures are seen as pointless. One reviewer found the high standards reasonable for future engineers.

ENGIN 29.summary: Reviews are overwhelmingly negative. Students describe disorganized assignments across several platforms, heavy workload, many exams and quizzes with no drops, and strict, unclear grading. A few say it is manageable and teaches sketching reasonably well. Most advise avoiding this instructor if possible.

ENGIN 40.summary: Students say the class is very disorganized, with disjointed lectures, a flawed textbook, long group homework of little exam relevance and changing grading schemes. Exam averages were failing and reportedly not curved. The instructor is described as kind, but reviewers mostly advise against it.

ENGIN 7.summary: Students praise this intro to Python and numerical methods as well organized, beginner friendly and useful. Weekly labs, discussions and homework are manageable, and exams are challenging but fair with clobber and extra credit. Reviewers advise attending office hours and doing the labs.

ENGLISH 117S.summary: Few reviews, mostly very positive about engaging, funny lecturers who make Shakespeare accessible. A few assignments make up the grade, so there is little room for error, and grading can be harsh depending on the GSI. Reviewers advise discussing papers with the instructor.

ENGLISH 118.summary: Reviewers describe inspiring, well-crafted lectures and a caring instructor. The class is demanding, with hard weekly quizzes, strictly graded essays and a heavy reading load. Students advise attending every lecture and using office hours for essays.

ENGLISH 45A.summary: Few reviews, mostly positive about engaging, approachable lectures and manageable reading, though early modern language takes effort. Instructors are described as supportive. One older review found lectures unnecessary and confusing, and GSI grading was called tough.

ENGLISH 45B.summary: Few reviews, mostly positive. Students say lectures are engaging, clear and funny, and instructors are kind and helpful. One reviewer was not a fan of the course content itself, and another noted easy midterms but hard papers.

ENVECON 100.summary: Students are very positive about the teaching, citing clear, funny lectures and an approachable instructor. The course is intermediate microeconomic theory, so expect real work, challenging exams and time-consuming online assignments. Reading the chapter before class and attending office hours are common advice.

EPS 7.summary: Students describe an easy, manageable breadth class with one online homework per week and exam questions drawn from it. Lectures are widely called engaging. Complaints center on strict deadlines with no extensions, where a few missed assignments can cost an A, and on slow replies to emails.

EPS 82.summary: Students agree it is an easy breadth thanks to lots of extra credit and a generous curve. Many complain that lectures are hard to hear and follow, the course is disorganized, communication and grading are slow, and exams do not match study materials. Not recommended for real interest in oceans.

EPS C20.summary: Reviewers find the content easy, the workload light, and the lectures interesting. Nearly all are angry that the final was switched from online and open-note to in-person and closed-note a few weeks before the exam, with little communication. Students warn the syllabus format may not hold.

ESPM 10.summary: Reviewers describe a fairly easy, low-stress class with interesting content and a kind instructor. Lectures are often called slow or stale, and exams can feel random compared to the study guide. Attendance and participation are required.

ESPM 140.summary: Students say this entomology course is rewarding for people who love insects but very demanding, largely because of the 100-family insect collection and visual memorization. Exams are described as hard but fair, and a prerequisite course is strongly advised. Lectures are passionate and interesting.

ESPM 15.summary: Students praise the engaging, funny lectures and say the class is not very hard, with light coursework. Repeated warning: exams are not common sense and can include tricky or very specific questions, so review notes and slides regularly. Office hours are described as helpful.

ESPM 165.summary: Students sharply disagree. Many call it life-changing, with real-world, critical perspectives on development and an engaged instructor. Others find lectures rambling and fast with no slides, unclear assignments and grading criteria, and a disorganized class. Expect to follow lectures closely.

ESPM 2.summary: Students describe an easy, interesting intro class with a broad scope, passionate teaching and detailed study guides. Exams and quizzes are mostly straightforward and online. Some note disorganization, occasional grading errors and slow email replies, plus mandatory discussion sections.

ESPM 42.summary: Students call this an interesting, fairly easy breadth class about insects with passionate teaching, field trips and projects. Exams rely on memorization of dense slides, with no homework or study guides. Several say the workload is heavy for 3 units, so it suits those actually interested in the subject.

ESPM 50AC.summary: Students describe a very easy, low-stress breadth class with light work and lenient grading. Lectures are widely called rambling or boring, so many watch recordings at higher speed. Attendance is mandatory, and most expect an A or A- with minimal effort.

ESPM 6.summary: Students overwhelmingly call this an easy breadth class with very light workload. Grades come from a few quizzes or papers plus a project and field activity, and attendance is optional. Many enjoy the discussion-style classes, though a few say they learned little. Reviewers say you get out what you put in.

ESPM C10.summary: Students say this is an easy breadth class with straightforward content and mostly easy exams. Lectures are often called boring, disorganized, or heavy on videos, and the instructor is slow to answer emails. Attendance and participation are tracked, slides are useful for studying, and readings are mostly optional.

FILM 10.summary: Students like the selection of early films and the enthusiastic, kind teaching. Many complain about disorganized lectures, unclear instructions, trivia-style weekly quizzes, very late grading and little guidance on papers and the final. Several reviewers found the class stressful, though some call it easy.

FILM 20.summary: Reviewers describe a very demanding lower-division theory course with heavy dense reading and grades based on two papers and two exams. Exams are memorization-heavy and grading feedback is slow. Many strongly advise against it, though a few say it is manageable with thorough notes.

FRENCH 80.summary: Students love the engaging, entertaining lectures and interesting films and readings. Expect substantial annotated reading, short writing assignments that can be redone, and exams needing real memorization with little study guidance. Reviewers say it is not an easy breadth but very rewarding.

GEOG 130.summary: Reviews are mixed. Some say the material is well explained and that coursework is easy to score on, while exams are the hardest part. Others find lectures dull, exam grading standards harsh and discussion sections weak. Reading load is substantial, and some terms used take-home essay exams.

GEOG 181.summary: Students love this field-based course with trips around the Bay Area, calling it inspiring and perspective-changing. The instructor is described as kind and engaged, with manageable, flexible assignments such as short responses, participation and a final project. Be ready for a lot of walking off campus.

GEOG 40.summary: Students say lectures are funny and engaging, but exams are harder and trickier than the lectures suggest. Lectures are information dense and tests can ask about single details. Many liked the class anyway, but several warn it is not an easy A.

GEOG 50AC.summary: Students say this is a well-liked American Cultures course with engaging, if sometimes rambling, lectures and a caring instructor. Workload is moderate, with a midterm, a final and a few projects or essays. Attendance is graded, and reading and note-taking lead to a good grade.

GEOG 70AC.summary: Students say lectures are interesting and clear and the instructor is caring and accessible. Assignments are fair, including reading responses and take-home essays. Reviewers describe it as an easy or manageable class if you attend lecture and keep up with readings.

GEOG N50AC.summary: Students say this is a well-liked American Cultures course with engaging, if sometimes rambling, lectures and a caring instructor. Workload is moderate, with a midterm, a final and a few projects or essays. Attendance is graded, and reading and note-taking lead to a good grade.

GLOBAL 100P.summary: Students find the topic fascinating and the instructor kind and helpful, with practical assignments like mock negotiations and presentations. Lectures are often described as dry or hard to follow and the reading load is heavy. Study guides closely match exams, so do the readings.

GLOBAL 10B.summary: Students report heavy weekly reading with short reading notes, and some lectures that are dry. Opinions vary by instructor, with some praising caring, fair teaching and others citing unclear paper expectations and harsh grading. Not an easy A, but exams are often manageable.

GLOBAL 132.summary: Reviews are mixed. Supporters enjoy the participation-heavy format with group projects, role-playing mediation and caring teaching. Critics say lectures are basic or disorganized and exams cover material not discussed in class. Attendance and participation matter, and exams are essay-based with heavy readings.

GLOBAL 150Q.summary: Reviewers mostly praise a discussion-based seminar where instructors learn your name and care about students. Expect weekly readings, short assignments, and a research paper. Some find grading picky, with strict word limits and little leniency on extensions. Lectures are not recorded, so attendance helps.

GLOBAL 173.summary: Students mostly enjoy the engaging, funny lectures and say the course is not too hard, with papers and an open-note final. Lectures are not recorded, so in-person attendance matters. One review says the instructor is hard to reach and a few mention unclear paper source requirements.

GLOBAL 45.summary: Students report a reading-heavy world history course with mandatory but random attendance, a no-technology policy and unrecorded lectures. Lectures are seen as knowledgeable but fast and sometimes dry, and the GSIs are widely praised. Exams are conceptual and manageable, and the required textbook is called not very useful.

GLOBAL C10A.summary: Students mostly enjoy this intro for its funny, passionate lectures and interesting topics. Workload is described as heavy reading plus papers, though some call it easy. Slides are not very helpful so attending lecture matters, and grades depend a lot on your GSI.

GPP 105.summary: Reviewers praise this seminar-style course on ethics and global practice for engaging discussion, interesting readings, and a caring, organized instructor. Work is essays and participation with no tests, and it is as hard as you make it. One review found lectures dull.

GWS 10.summary: Students call this a manageable, interesting breadth class with heavy reading that lectures largely recap. Writing assignments and easy exams determine the grade. Many praise the instructor's passion, though some find lectures long, repetitive or tangent-heavy. Keeping up with readings helps on assignments.

GWS 100AC.summary: Reviewers disagree, with many calling the lectures insightful and the readings fascinating, while others find them repetitive and the grading picky. Expect heavy reading, many assignments and mandatory attendance. Several say the topics focus on settler colonialism, and some suggest other American Cultures options.

GWS 102.summary: Reviews vary a lot by instructor. Recent students describe light workload, discussion posts, a short paper, and a final paper, with caring teaching. Older reviews report scattered lectures, dense readings that were not unpacked, strict class rules, and unclear grading criteria.

GWS 129.summary: Students generally enjoy the interesting readings and passionate, caring instruction. Exams are described as essay based and fairly easy, and grading is lenient, though keeping up with readings is needed. A recent review found lectures disorganized and slides posted late.

GWS 130AC.summary: Students describe a light workload of weekly reading responses and notes, with interesting, thought-provoking lectures. Grading is clear and not harsh, and attendance counts for a large share. Reviewers say it is close to an easy A if you attend and do the assignments.

GWS 14.summary: Students say lectures are excellent and tie material to current events. The workload is described as manageable, mainly readings, plus an essay, reading responses and a final project. Reading is heavy but not all needs to be completed. Reviewers strongly recommend the class.

GWS 20.summary: Students like this feminist theory intro for its interesting readings, discussion, and a caring instructor. Lectures can be talkative or less engaging, and the reading is sometimes dense. A few assignments with vague instructions make up the grade, so do not miss any. Grading is described as generous.

GWS 50AC.summary: Students call this a fairly easy American Cultures course with interesting content but a lot of long weekly readings. Exams are often take-home or open note and grading is described as lenient. Lectures get mixed reviews, from passionate to repetitive, and some say grading and organization are inconsistent.

HISTORY 160.summary: Reviewers mostly like the lectures and content, though a few find them hard to follow or read from slides. Grading is test-heavy and described as clear and fair, with questions given beforehand. A couple of reviews found it unclear and not worthwhile.

HISTORY 20.summary: Most students find the lectures excellent and the class rewarding but not an easy breadth. It is reading heavy, with several papers and discussion participation. Attending lecture and taking notes is essential, since slides are not helpful. A few found lectures and readings hard to follow.

HISTORY 4A.summary: Reviewers praise engaging, well-organized lectures and say to take detailed notes since slides are sparse. The grade rests on papers and exams with few chances to boost it, so it can be harder to earn an A than expected. Reading load is large, and your GSI affects the experience.

HISTORY 7A.summary: Students find lectures engaging and passionate, but they are not recorded and slides are sparse, so good notes are essential. The grade rests on a few essays and exams, graded harshly by some GSIs, and the reading load is heavy. Reviewers disagree on whether it is worth taking as a breadth.

HISTORY 7B.summary: Students say the lectures are well constructed and often eye-opening, but note heavy weekly reading and strict, section-dependent grading. Reviewers disagree on the lecturer, with some loving the course and others finding it boring or biased. It is not an easy A, so STEM-heavy students are advised to take it Pass/No Pass.

IAS N45.summary: Students call it a favorite, with fascinating, well-connected lectures covering a lot of world history. It is a lot of reading, with challenging but fair tests and essays, and a strict no phones or laptops rule. A good discussion section leader matters for your grade.

INDENG 115.summary: Students are very positive, citing clear lectures, fair exams and a useful database curriculum including SQL. The semester-long group project with a real client is time consuming but widely called rewarding. Some find quizzes and labs weaker or poorly worded.

INTEGBI 11.summary: Students describe an easy, enjoyable breadth class with interesting lectures, field trips and project-based assignments instead of exams. Attendance is often optional and grading is fair, though feedback can be slow. Reviewers strongly recommend it.

INTEGBI 35AC.summary: Students call this an easy, interesting breadth that satisfies life science and American Cultures requirements. Lectures are described as engaging, quizzes and exams are often open note, and the workload is light. Attendance checks and a final essay or project count, so show up and do the assignments.

ISF 100A.summary: Most reviewers praise thought-provoking lectures, excellent but difficult readings and an accessible, caring instructor. The teaching style is unconventional and sometimes unstructured, and a few found lectures dry or slides poor. Exams are curved, and GSI study guides help.

ISF 100B.summary: Students praise inspiring lectures, clear grading, and a supportive instructor. The reading load is very heavy, and reviewers advise attending lecture and reading only the parts discussed. Exam content is shared in advance and the class is curved, so most describe it as manageable.

ISF 100D.summary: Students find the books and discussions interesting and the class easy to do well in if you attend, with open-note exams. Common complaints are heavy reading, unstructured lectures, unclear grading criteria, and exam or essay details revealed late. Opinions are mixed but mostly positive.

LEGALST 160.summary: Reviewers disagree sharply. Fans call it one of the best classes, with detailed lectures and strong law school preparation, while critics find it stressful and strict. Expect 50 to 100 pages of reading weekly, required participation and tough exams. Doing the readings and attending lecture is the repeated advice.

LEGALST 184.summary: Students agree it is a lot of work, with long readings, annotations and detailed exams. Many find it rewarding, well organized and clearly graded, and say effort leads to good grades. Others find it overwhelming, with no slides posted, dry delivery and a rigid style. Office hours help.

LINGUIS 100.summary: Students say the weekly homework is hard and time consuming, while lectures are funny and interesting and exams are fairly straightforward. Recent reviews mention four midterms plus a final and nitpicky grading. Reviewers say it is hard to track your grade and that the work is worth it for those interested.

LINGUIS 130.summary: Students describe a hard but rewarding course with excellent, funny lectures. Weekly homework is demanding and tedious, but reviewers mention generous curves and grade cutoffs. Attending lecture, section and office hours is advised, since handouts alone are not enough.

MATH 104.summary: Reviewers describe a hard but rewarding analysis course with rigorous lectures, many office hours, and often generous curving. Grading is described as strict, and a few found the instructor condescending or the exams unlike the practice ones. Most still call it one of their best math classes.

MATH 105.summary: Few reviews describe the course itself. Students say it is extremely hard with brutal homework and difficult exams, but that the curve can be generous and the second half on measure theory is more forgiving. Office hours are helpful and working with classmates is recommended. Several reviews are off topic.

MATH 10A.summary: Reviewers are strongly negative about this offering. They report confusing lectures, no recordings, very heavy homework, and exams that do not resemble homework or practice tests. Many say the textbook helps more than lecture, and prior calculus experience makes it easier. Few positive comments appear.

MATH 10B.summary: Most reviews are strongly negative about past semesters. Students report no syllabus, very late grading, canceled classes and harsh, unclear grading, with tests making up nearly all of the grade. The content itself is described as manageable. One recent review mentions a lenient curve and practice tests help.

MATH 110.summary: Reviews disagree sharply by instructor. Some find the course fair, with helpful materials and generous partial credit. Others call it too computational for an upper-division class, with heavy homework, fast or cluttered lectures, and harsh curves. Students say grading and the curve matter a lot.

MATH 113.summary: Reviews are mixed and vary a lot by instructor. Some describe accessible, clear teaching with fair exams and quick grading, while others report disorganization, fast pacing, unclear lectures and heavy self-study. Review sheets and office hours help where offered.

MATH 115.summary: Students find the topics interesting and the instructor friendly and available, but the lectures are described as freestyle and disorganized. Midterms and finals are called hard or even brutal, and some homework needed outside research. Reviews are mixed and fairly old.

MATH 124.summary: Students highly recommend this programming course for math majors with little coding experience. They describe well-organized materials, clear grading, fair tests and interesting but sometimes challenging homework and projects. The instructor is supportive, and reviewers advise reading the notes and attending office hours.

MATH 128A.summary: Most reviewers are negative, citing disorganized instruction, unhelpful lectures and practice materials, exams that go beyond what was taught, and slow communication. Grades lean heavily on exams. A few found the material manageable and the lectures excellent with another instructor.

MATH 151.summary: Reviews are sharply split by era. Older reviews describe fair tests, in-depth lectures and helpful office hours, with content that takes practice. A recent review describes a disorganized course with no syllabus, unclear tests, and content unrelated to teaching. Experience appears to depend heavily on the instructor.

MATH 160.summary: Students describe an enjoyable, engaging course with interesting lectures, accessible office hours and fair, sometimes easy exams. Homework is usually manageable, and group work at the board is common. Reviewers recommend it for the enthusiasm and approachable teaching.

MATH 16A.summary: Reviews are split and depend heavily on the instructor. Some praise caring, clear teaching, while others find lectures fast and tests unlike the homework. Many say you must teach yourself, especially without prior calculus. Nearly everyone mentions a generous curve, and office hours and tutoring are recommended.

MATH 16B.summary: Reviews are mixed and depend heavily on the instructor. Midterms are generally described as reasonable, while finals are often much harder than practice material, though curves tend to be generous. Students recommend understanding the homework and quizzes, using office hours, and note that review materials can be harder than exams.

MATH 185.summary: Reviews are mostly negative. Students describe unclear, rushed or tangent-filled lectures, heavy homework, very difficult quizzes with low averages, and unhelpful office hours. A few say the textbook and clear materials make it manageable, and grading and curves vary. Summer sections drew particular complaints.

MATH 1A.summary: Reviews vary sharply by instructor. Some students describe clear lectures, manageable work and caring teaching with drops available. Others report heavy homework, a final worth a large share of the grade, pointless labs and poor organization. Going to office hours is a repeated tip.

MATH 1B.summary: Students say experiences depend heavily on the instructor. Some praise clear, concise lectures and a fair curve, while others find lectures fast and confusing and end up self-studying. Exams are often described as harder than practice material, and several mention heavy homework.

MATH 51.summary: Students say lectures are fast, disorganized and hard to follow, so many teach themselves from notes, practice exams and YouTube. Prior calculus experience helps a lot. Exams are heavily weighted, but the curve is generous and the provided notes and practice exams are praised.

MATH 52.summary: Reviews are sharply split by instructor. Some students praise clear lectures, fair exams, helpful office hours and a generous curve. Others describe heavy homework, hard-to-follow lectures, strict grading that deducts for showing work, and a largely self-taught course.

MATH 53.summary: Students describe a difficult, homework-heavy course where exams resemble homework but the final is harder. Reviews split on grading: some report a fair curve, others a strict scale with no curve and practice exams that do not match. Lectures vary a lot by instructor, and many advise doing all the homework.

MATH 54.summary: Students say the content is manageable but lectures vary a lot by instructor, and many recommend self-studying from the textbook or online videos. Homework is light, exams match homework and practice material, and generous curves are common. Some find the course computation-heavy and the differential equations algebra messy.

MATH 55.summary: Students describe a difficult, proof-heavy course with long homework, but most find lectures clear and exams fair with generous curving. Extra credit and clobber-style policies help. Reviewers advise attending lecture, reading the textbook and practicing. A few say lectures can be confusing.

MATH 56.summary: Students say lectures are clear, conceptual and well liked, and the instructor and GSIs are supportive. Workload can be high, with quizzes, homework, projects and exams. The textbook was new and had errors, and some found exams computation-heavy compared with lectures.

MATH H104.summary: Students call this possibly the hardest and most abstract class at Berkeley, with an enormous workload and very long, tangent-filled lectures. Many say it was the most they ever learned and was well worth it, while others found the lectures disorganized and the pace overwhelming. Expect extreme intensity and high attrition.

MATH H110.summary: Students say this is a hard, theoretical class with tough exams, low averages, and strict partial credit. Reviewers disagree on teaching: some find lectures clear and instructors caring and accessible, while recent reviews report unclear lectures, heavy homework, and harsh curving. Office hours are widely recommended.

MATH H113.summary: Reviews are polarized. Fans say the course is demanding but opens up real mathematics with excellent lectures and notes, though homework can be heavy. Critics describe disorganized teaching, no clear grading criteria and unhelpful office hours. Experience varies a lot by instructor.

MATH H53.summary: Reviews are split. Some enjoy the conceptual, proof-oriented approach and clear explanations, and note generous curves. Others say lectures are slow on basics then rushed, or move too quickly into proofs, so self-study from the textbook is needed. Grades rest mostly on tests, so do the unassigned homework.

MATH N16A.summary: Students say lectures are fast and hard to follow, so the class is largely self-taught, with weekly quizzes and exams that are harder than homework. Many describe a generous curve and a caring, very responsive instructor. Experiences depend on prior calculus background, and office hours help.

MATH N16B.summary: Students say lectures vary in clarity but the instructor is very accessible and responsive. The class is tough but doable, with weekly quizzes, generous curves, and exams that follow homework and review sheets, though review sheets can be harder than exams. It takes significant time, and self-discipline helps.

MATH N1A.summary: Reviews are older and describe an easy calculus class if you do the homework and practice exams. Most say lectures are tangent-filled and not essential, so you largely teach yourself. Quizzes depend on your GSI and the final can be tricky. Prior calculus makes it much easier.

MATH N1B.summary: Reviews are older and say the lectures are unhelpful, so students learn from the book, GSI and homework, which counts for a large share of the grade. The class is described as fairly easy with a curve, though the second midterm was notably harder. Practice exams help.

MATH N53.summary: Reviews are mixed and mostly older. Many call lectures clear and entertaining, but exams are widely described as very hard, especially a final worth about half the grade. A curve helps. Reviewers advise doing many practice problems and going to office hours.

MATH W128A.summary: Students say lectures are clear and engaging, with a clear syllabus and fair homework and exams. Some report that quizzes included topics not covered in problem sets and that the online format was confusing. Programming assignments and instructor help are well regarded.

MATH W53.summary: Students describe an online multivariable calculus class that is generally manageable, with lots of drops, clear grading and fair quizzes and finals. Lectures are often pre-recorded and office hours are important. Grades depend partly on the GSI. One recent honors-section review found it proof-heavy and far harder than expected.

MATH W54.summary: Reviewers strongly praise the instructor's responsiveness, many office hours, and good study resources. Lectures are described as dry or abstract, and exams and weekly quizzes can be hard. The curve and grade cutoffs are widely called generous, with grade bins adjusted when exams run difficult.

MATSCI 45.summary: Most reviews are negative, describing confusing lectures read from slides, exams with material not yet taught, late homework grading and little practice material. Students teach themselves from the textbook, and a curve helps. A few found the workload manageable and the class enjoyable.

MCELLBI 135A.summary: Students love this experiment-focused endocrinology course and its engaging teaching. It uses a course reader instead of slides, with open-note application-based exams and weekly discussion work. Some find the structure loose, studying unusual, and lectures hard to follow at first, but most say it is fair and worth taking.

MCELLBI 136.summary: Students say the course covers a lot of detailed material with moderately tricky exams and some memorization. Lecture quality is described as inconsistent, with some finding it inspiring and others disorganized or rushed. Reviewers recommend reading the textbook and going to office hours.

MCELLBI 150.summary: Reviewers, all from older terms, say lectures are clear, well organized and engaging. They note a heavy load of information, problem sets that can be harder than the exam, and no easy A. Reviewing the textbook before lecture and understanding the concepts is advised.

MCELLBI 165.summary: Reviewers mostly love this engaging, funny lecture course on drugs and the brain, calling it interesting and one of the easier upper-division MCB classes. Take detailed notes and study the reader. Some say lectures are unstructured and exams include obscure facts or memorization.

MCELLBI 32.summary: Reviewers call this a very heavy, memorization-based class with lots of content for an intro course. Exams are hard with low averages and no curve, though course modules and extra credit help. Many advise against taking it just for breadth, and say it takes a lot of study time.

MCELLBI 38.summary: Students call it beginner friendly with engaging lectures, posted notes, recorded lectures and light weekly homework. Exams carry most of the grade, require a lot of memorization, and have no curve. Some found one lecturer's teaching denser than the other's.

MCELLBI 50.summary: Students find the immunology lectures engaging and the instructor knowledgeable, but the course is challenging. Exams make up most of the grade and are hard but fair, lectures move quickly, and iClicker participation matters. Reviewers advise studying hard and using office hours.

MCELLBI 55.summary: Students say the lectures are engaging and the instructors accessible, but the class is memorization-heavy and harder than a typical breadth. Clicker attendance matters and exams reward steady studying, with a curve. Some recent reviewers advise Pass/No Pass unless you like biology.

MCELLBI C100A.summary: Reviewers praise clear, well-organized lectures with detailed notes and fair exams. The course is tough, with lots of material, hard problem sets and time-pressured tests. Students advise doing all problem sets and practice exams, going to tutoring and GSI office hours, and reading the textbook.

MECENG 100.summary: Reviewers mostly say lectures teach little and the course is disorganized, with GSIs and discussions carrying the learning. Labs and the final project are praised as fun and useful. Exams vary, with some very hard take-home tests. Students advise self-studying and relying on staff.

MECENG 103.summary: Reviewers are strongly negative. They say lectures cover little useful material, the course is run largely by GSIs, and grading and project expectations are unclear and punitive. Students report having to teach themselves and advise avoiding it with this instructor if you can.

MECENG 135.summary: Reviews are mixed. The class is mostly open labs and a large open-ended project in LabVIEW, where you get out what you put in. Some find the instructor helpful in lab, while others say lectures teach little and offer no help with projects.

MECENG 40.summary: Students describe a tough thermodynamics class with difficult exams, MATLAB-based homework and few practice exams. Many say attending lecture is key to doing well, and some find lectures thorough while others find them bare. Reviews are split, with several strongly negative about the course experience.

MECENG C85.summary: Reviews are mixed. Many say the class is easy and the exams fair, with problems hinted ahead of time, while others find lectures hard to follow and feel they had to teach themselves. Homework is reasonable and counts for a good share of the grade. Several say it is an easy A but weak for learning the material.

MEDIAST 111.summary: Students report an overwhelming amount of reading, disorganized lectures, and difficult exams that test obscure details. Clicker quizzes and harsh grading draw complaints, and extra credit is seen as minimal. A few say it is rewarding if you stay engaged and use office hours. Reviews are strongly negative.

MEDIAST 112.summary: Students find it challenging but rewarding, with engaging, humorous lectures and helpful office hours. Success depends on taking notes, completing study guides and studying ahead. Lectures move fast, and the grade includes two papers, a midterm and a final.

MEDIAST 113.summary: Most reviewers are strongly negative, citing disorganized lectures and slides, confusing assignment instructions, heavy weekly group work, and unclear or slow grading. Some say the topic is interesting and one called it a favorite and worthwhile. Many skip lecture and rely on readings and discussion sections.

MELC 18.summary: Students describe a chill survey of Ancient Egypt with light workload and engaging subject matter, though lectures can be dry and fast. Reviews disagree on exams: some find them easy, others say you must memorize over 100 terms. Discussion sections and GSIs are praised.

MUSIC 128.summary: Reviewers, mostly from older terms, call the lectures highly entertaining and eloquent, and the grading generous. One reviewer felt the later course material became repetitive and that final essay advice was ambiguous. Overall the class is described as an enjoyable one for music students.

MUSIC 151A.summary: Reviews are largely negative. Students describe a demanding, strict class with required attendance and constant participation, and many say the instructor is harsh or condescending when answers are slow. Some note he knows the subject well, and that it may help if you can answer basics quickly.

MUSIC 26AC.summary: Reviews are sharply split. Some find it interesting and easy, while many say lectures are slow and boring, policies strict, and quizzes obscure. Readings, no-device rules and mandatory discussion participation come up often. Several warn against taking it as an easy breadth.

MUSIC 27.summary: Students describe an easy, enjoyable breadth class with engaging lectures, short weekly writing, and fair exams. Going to lecture and discussion section is the repeated advice, and the textbook is rarely needed. Many call it an easy A, though some note fussy grading on essays.

MUSIC N26AC.summary: Reviews are mixed but lean negative. Some find the lectures interesting and the class light, while many describe boring long lectures, strict policies, no devices and hard, specific quizzes. Reviewers say it has become harder than its easy-breadth reputation, and several suggest another AC course.

NWMEDIA 151AC.summary: Students disagree on this American Cultures course. Some say the content is easy and grading generous, while others describe harsh, unexplained point deductions, little written feedback and a heavy load of presentations and research in a short span. Assignments are tracked closely for AI use.

PHILOS 100.summary: Students describe a demanding course with a short essay due every week, dense readings, and a large final paper. Several report it as a heavy time commitment and say lectures were hard to follow. Opinions on the instructor differ, and GSI help was said to come late.

PHILOS 12A.summary: Students call this a difficult logic course driven by time-consuming weekly problem sets, with fair homework and midterm but a final many describe as much harder. Lectures are often dry or hard to follow, so sections, office hours, and study groups are strongly advised. Those with math strength fare better.

PHILOS 132.summary: Reviews split sharply. Some say the explanations of hard concepts are excellent and engaging. Others say lectures are unprepared, rambling, and without slides or notes, leaving little learned. Several mention a heavy reading load of 100 or more pages a week.

PHILOS 135.summary: Students say lectures are exceptionally clear and the content fascinating, but the readings are difficult and the course is dense and not for beginners. Section instructors tend to grade tough, and recording lectures is suggested. A few reviews are negative about grading.

PHILOS 2.summary: Students describe an enjoyable, interesting class with a passionate instructor and relatively light work. Readings can be tricky but lectures clarify them, and discussion participation matters. It is recommended as a breadth, with the final essay the hardest part.

PHILOS 25A.summary: Students find lectures clear and the material interesting, but the course is demanding for an intro. Expect a lot of reading, reading quizzes, and tough essay grading that depends heavily on your GSI. Reviewers advise keeping up with readings, using the study questions, and attending discussion.

PHILOS 25B.summary: Students say lectures are clear, thorough and enjoyable and break down dense readings well. The course is reading-heavy with three essays and a final, and your grade depends largely on your GSI. Reviewers advise doing at least some of the readings and using the study guide.

PHILOS 3.summary: Students find it an engaging, funny and easy-going intro to philosophy with a reasonable workload. Grading is mostly essays, section participation and a final. Grading speed and quality depend heavily on the GSI, and the readings take time to digest.

PHYSED 1.summary: Students describe a motivating, well-structured activity class where the instructor is encouraging and pushes you to improve. Workouts get harder, early sections are tough to wake up for, and attendance is strictly enforced with make-ups. Beginners and experienced students both benefit.

PHYSICS 137A.summary: Students call this a very hard, theory-heavy quantum course with long, difficult exams, but a good curve. Many praise the lecture notes, fair exams, and accessible help, while others find the lectures abstract or confusing. Reviewers say to refresh linear algebra and vector calculus beforehand.

PHYSICS 5A.summary: Reviews are divided. Some find lectures rigorous and clear, while others find them confusing and say homework is extremely long and typo-ridden. Exams are hard with averages near 50 percent, but students report generous curves and partial credit. Expect a challenging, theory-heavy course.

PHYSICS 5B.summary: Students praise clear lectures and excellent posted lecture notes, light homework with flexible deadlines and plenty of practice problems. Exams are hard, often harder than practice ones, and lectures can feel rushed near the end. Studying derivations is a common tip.

PHYSICS 7A.summary: Students say the course is tough, with a steep learning curve and hard exams, but generous grade bins and curves. Lectures, notes and practice exams are widely praised for helping, though quality varies by instructor. Keeping up with homework and practice tests is the common advice.

PHYSICS 7B.summary: Students say lectures are intuitive for many, but exams are very hard with low averages, short formula sheets and limited partial credit. Curves are often described as generous, though some disagree. Attending lecture, doing practice exams and textbook problems, and keeping up with the fast pace are the repeated advice.

PHYSICS 7C.summary: Reviewers describe clear, engaging, supportive lectures and say 7C is the most interesting of the series. Exams are generally fair and resemble the plentiful practice material, though they require real studying. A couple of older reviews mention uneven exam difficulty and harsh rubrics.

PHYSICS 8A.summary: Students say the class is entertaining and approachable even without prior physics, though exams are tough and often differ from practice tests. Homework is seen as less useful than practice exams. Reviewers mention generous curving and grade bins, and advise self-study and lots of practice problems.

PHYSICS 8B.summary: Reviews depend heavily on the instructor. Some semesters are described as fair, engaging and generous with grades. Others are described as having unclear lectures, disorganized materials, difficult exams with low medians and many drops. Students suggest using the textbook and checking who is teaching.

POLECON 100.summary: Students say the readings are interesting but heavy, while lectures are often dry. Grades depend largely on the GSI, with participation counting and exams determining much of the grade. Some praise the course ideas, others cite unclear grading and little feedback.

POLECON 101.summary: Students generally praise knowledgeable, approachable instructors and helpful GSIs. The class is reading-heavy and lectures can be dry, but readings are broken down in lecture and section. Grading depends on your GSI and participation counts for a good part. A few found some lecturers biased.

POLECON 106.summary: Most reviewers describe a very hard, math-heavy microeconomics course with long problem sets, long exams, low midterm averages, and no curve. Many say lectures are hard to follow and the instructor is unsympathetic, and some recommend ECON 100A instead. A minority found it rewarding and say it taught them the most.

POLECON 107.summary: Students describe a very hard, lecture-heavy class with no-notes exams and a heavy memorization expectation. Many praise clear explanations and helpful office hours, while others cite disorganized lectures, little exam prep, limited recordings and inflexibility. Reviewers say success takes serious effort and a good section instructor.

POLSCI 1.summary: Reviewers are largely negative, citing exams that do not match lectures or study materials, unclear grading and a stressful final. Several say the section instructor largely determines your grade, and prior AP Government helps. A few found the content easy and the quizzes participation-based.

POLSCI 103.summary: Students say this is an interesting, well-structured course with clear grading, two short papers, a midterm and an optional final. Lectures are described as informative and recorded, and attendance is optional though recommended. A couple of reviews mention paper instructions that conflicted between lecture and sections.

POLSCI 109M.summary: Students say the class is discussion-based and theory heavy, with mandatory attendance and participation. Readings are central, but exam prompts are given in advance, with two midterms, a final and a group project. Reviews split between those who find it fun and rewarding and those who find it difficult or too theoretical.

POLSCI 111AC.summary: Students find the class interesting, connecting American political history to current events with film clips. Attendance is mandatory, and grades rest on three papers and participation. Reading is substantial, and lectures are sometimes read aloud from text and can feel confusing or dull. Most reviewers recommend it.

POLSCI 112C.summary: Students say lectures are unstructured and seminar-like, and attendance is optional, so the course suits self-motivated learners. Grades come from section participation and a few short papers, with no exams. Reviewers praise the instructor's passion, accessibility and writing feedback, but note heavy reading and weak lecture organization.

POLSCI 116W.summary: Students say the instructor is kind, passionate and helpful, but the material is dense with a lot of reading. GSIs are described as picky about writing. Some find lectures helpful and the class enjoyable, while others find it disorganized and not beginner-friendly.

POLSCI 124A.summary: Reviewers consistently call this one of their favorite classes, with engaging lectures and interesting readings. The workload is heavy on reading, and the instructor welcomes debate. Exams are essay based, with prompts often given early, and you need to write the way the grader expects.

POLSCI 124C.summary: Students describe a reading-heavy, theory-heavy class with dense but rewarding lectures. Grading uses reading quizzes, section participation, a midterm and a long research paper, with the paper needing early work and a good GSI. Most recommend it, though a few found it dry.

POLSCI 138E.summary: Students say this is an engaging but very dense political economy course with a large volume of reading and many theorists to remember. Assessments include papers, exams or in-class essays, and participation, and grading can depend on the GSI. Many call it one of their best classes, though some find it very hard.

POLSCI 141A.summary: Most students praise entertaining, passionate lectures and helpful office hours. The workload is reading-heavy, with weekly reading quizzes, study guides, and mandatory attendance. A couple of reviews mention long rants, going over time, and poor accessibility or accommodations.

POLSCI 141C.summary: Students say the material is interesting and the instructor knowledgeable, with fair but difficult exams. Lectures are old-school and can be dull or hard to follow. Reviews are mixed on helpfulness. Doing the readings and attending lecture are repeatedly advised.

POLSCI 143B.summary: Most reviewers praise witty, engaging lectures on Japanese politics, but note heavy reading, mandatory attendance because slides are not posted, and pop quizzes some find tough. Study guides are helpful and one bad quiz will not sink your grade. A few found lectures dry and the memorization burdensome.

POLSCI 144.summary: Students describe an extremely heavy reading load, arbitrary pop quizzes, early-morning dense lectures and hard exams with changing formats, with grades varying by section instructor. A minority praise the expertise and interesting content. Many warn against taking it without background in the subject.

POLSCI 145A.summary: Students say the course is insightful but reading heavy, with tough exams that make up much of the grade. Attendance and keeping up with the readings are strongly advised. Some older reviews criticized attendance policies and a flipped format, while others praised the expertise.

POLSCI 149E.summary: Students describe an entertaining, easy-workload class with light reading. The grade rests on a few essays and an exam or midterm. Several say essay grading is harsh and the course can feel shallow, but most recommend it.

POLSCI 149W.summary: Reviewers say the content is not hard and grades rest on a few exams and participation, but the 3-hour lectures drag on. Many find lectures disorganized and not well matched to exams. Some enjoyed the topic and engaging stories, while others raised concerns about perceived bias.

POLSCI 179.summary: Students see this one-unit pass/no pass guest-speaker course as an easy credit with low time commitment. The grade rests on a single final exam that is easy to pass but can ask very specific details. Laptops are banned, and opinions split on whether lectures are fun or overhyped.

POLSCI 181.summary: Students describe a reading-heavy but interesting course with short reading responses due before each class and take-home papers instead of exams. Lectures can be dry, and a few found grading harsh or feedback slow. Most find the course well organized and the instructor approachable.

POLSCI 186.summary: Students describe a manageable course with weekly reading responses, a midterm paper and a final paper. Lectures are seen as dry or boring, and attendance is taken, but there is no separate discussion section. Reviewers call it fairly easy and the instructor approachable.

POLSCI 2.summary: Students mostly love the engaging lectures and strongly recommend the course, while noting heavy reading, mandatory attendance and a strict no-technology rule. Essay prompts are released before exams, which makes studying straightforward. A minority say lectures drift into the instructor's own theories and repeat.

POLSCI 3.summary: Reviews are split. Some enjoy the flipped format with video lectures and coding assignments and find it organized and encouraging. Others say videos are confusing, exams do not match what was taught, grading and the curve are not transparent, and staff support is thin. Teaching assistant quality matters a lot.

POLSCI 4.summary: Reviewers overwhelmingly praise the lectures as clear, organized, and engaging, though no slides are used so careful notes matter. Readings are demanding but lectures explain them, and sections help. Grading is reported as fair, though one found it unclear.

POLSCI 5.summary: Students generally find the lectures engaging and the class manageable but reading-heavy, though readings can often be skimmed. Attendance is strongly advised since recordings and slides are limited. Grading depends on a few writing assignments and exams, is described as tough or unclear, and varies with the GSI.

POLSCI C135.summary: Students say this online game theory course has engaging video lectures but abstract material that gets hard to follow, and the textbook is little help. Expect many readings, quizzes and problem sets, with a curve. Falling behind is risky in an online format.

POLSCI W135.summary: Students describe an online game theory course with clear, engaging video lectures but abstract material that gets hard by the end. Quizzes and problem sets are challenging and not closely tied to lectures, though a curve helps. Expect many readings and assignments, and use online office hours.
