POLSCI W145A.summary: Reviews describe a reading-heavy course where exams make up most of the grade and are difficult. Many value the instructor's expertise and say doing the readings and attending discussion pays off. Others complain about the attendance policy and the flipped format used in some semesters.

POLSCI W3.summary: Students report a disorganized course with confusing lectures, error-prone exams and tests that do not match study guides. Many say they relied on summer videos, the GSI, the textbook or prior statistics knowledge. Office hours help, and the content itself is considered fairly simple.

PSYCH 1.summary: Reviewers say this is an easy, well-organized intro with engaging lectures, three straightforward papers, and fair exams drawn from slides and lecture. Attend lecture, since some material is not on slides and recordings are unreliable. Extra credit and a dropped test help; a few exam questions are very specific.

PSYCH 101.summary: Reviewers are overwhelmingly positive, saying the instructor makes statistics and R coding approachable even for people with no coding background. The workload is described as manageable, and exams and the final project as fair. Advice is to keep up with work and ask for help early, since it is easy to get lost.

PSYCH 150.summary: Students generally love this class, calling lectures funny, clear, and engaging, with fair exams and doable weekly work. Reviewers describe it as easy to moderate, with long readings and time-consuming web exercises. Extra credit is common, and most say to study the slides and not underestimate the multiple choice.

PSYCH 156.summary: Reviews are mixed, with many praising interesting content and lectures. The grade rests almost entirely on a few exams, so one bad exam can hurt, and sections are called pointless. Several mention disorganized lectures, harsh or uneven GSI grading, and exams drawn heavily from the book.

PSYCH 160.summary: Students say the lectures are engaging and the material interesting, but the grade rests mostly on a few exams that are harder than they look. Reading the textbook carefully and studying the long study guides are repeated advice. Most recommend it, though some found exam questions wordy.

PSYCH C120.summary: Few reviews, mostly positive about entertaining lectures, interesting topics and generous curving. Exams use the slides, and attendance matters less. Complaints include a vague group project and weekly quizzes that can be tricky and heavily weighted.

PSYCH C61.summary: Few reviews, but students find the lectures passionate and the subject interesting. Exams are described as easy or open note, yet they test small details from lectures and the textbook. Reviewers advise reading consistently and not falling behind.

PSYCH N150.summary: Students generally love this class, calling lectures funny, clear, and engaging, with fair exams and doable weekly work. Reviewers describe it as easy to moderate, with long readings and time-consuming web exercises. Extra credit is common, and most say to study the slides and not underestimate the multiple choice.

PSYCH N160.summary: Reviews are positive and describe engaging, clear lectures with class exercises. Exams are called easy to fair and based on lecture notes, with extra credit available. Only a few reviews exist, and most are older.

PUBPOL 141.summary: Reviews are mixed. The behavioral economics content is called interesting, with short quizzes, a few projects, no midterm, and dropped low scores. Complaints include disorganization, unclear expectations, late or missing grades, and required attendance with an iClicker remote.

SLAVIC 49AC.summary: Students describe a light, enjoyable class built around reading roughly one children's book a week, with easy, mostly in-class writing. The instructor is kind and accommodating, and lectures are sometimes surface-level. Reviewers recommend it for the American Cultures requirement.

SOCIOL 1.summary: Most reviewers enjoy this intro, praising engaging lectures, manageable work, and fair, fairly easy exams. Common complaints are lengthy readings, boring lectures for some, vague project rubrics, and grades that vary by GSI. Students advise going to lecture and doing the readings.

SOCIOL 101.summary: Students describe a dense, reading-heavy theory course, with lectures that most find engaging and important for understanding. Discussion sections and a good GSI help a lot, and quizzes can be tricky. Opinions on how approachable and clear the lecturer is vary by semester.

SOCIOL 102.summary: Reviews conflict. Some praise clear, insightful explanations of hard theory and helpful office hours. Others find lectures confusing and disorganized, readings long, and papers demanding. Many say the section instructor is critical to doing well. An A takes real work, though a B range is more manageable.

SOCIOL 110.summary: Students say the lectures are clear and engaging and the course is manageable if you attend or use the slides. Assessments are take-home midterms, reading responses and a final that many call hard. Reviewers complain about unclear rubrics and harsh grading by readers, with some calling it a low-effort A.

SOCIOL 111AC.summary: Students say the instructor is kind and caring and the topics are interesting, with essays, take-home or written exams and random attendance checks. Reading is heavy and lectures can be repetitive or tangent-filled. Grading by section instructors is described as inconsistent and sometimes harsh.

SOCIOL 114.summary: Students mostly find it a rewarding, eye-opening class on legal theory with engaging lectures and fair, lenient grading. The material can be difficult. Lectures are recorded and attendance is not taken. A few reviewers felt the instructor pushed personal opinions.

SOCIOL 117.summary: Students generally call this an easy, interesting class on sports and society with an enthusiastic lecturer. Attending lectures and doing some reading is enough for a good grade. Complaints include an overly specific final, tricky multiple-choice quizzes, vague instructions and strict rounding.

SOCIOL 121.summary: Reviews are strongly divided. Some find the lectures inspiring and the workload easy, while many describe unclear instructions, subjective grading and a rude or condescending tone. No electronics are allowed, attendance is mandatory, and exams depend on fast note-taking.

SOCIOL 127.summary: Most students find lectures engaging and the grading forgiving, with low-stakes quizzes, essays, extra credit for participation and clear rubrics. Readings are long and papers involve independent research, graded tougher by section instructors. Many call it an easy A with good notes. A couple of reviews object to lecture content.

SOCIOL 130.summary: Reviews are split. A summer version was called easy, simple and interesting, but most reviewers describe unclear instructions, subjective grading and a condescending tone. Some say disagreeing with the instructor's viewpoint hurts grades, and one cited a low class average on the final.

SOCIOL 130AC.summary: Reviews are mixed. Some find the content interesting and the instructor approachable, saying exams follow the study guides if you do the readings. Others call lectures boring and disconnected from the assignments, with unclear instructions and tough grading by readers. Expect a lot of reading.

SOCIOL 133.summary: Students say lectures are clear, organized and engaging, and the readings interesting. Workload is light, mostly readings, reading responses and take-home essays, with clear rubrics. Grading depends on the reader and can be tough but with good feedback. Attending lecture and office hours is advised.

SOCIOL 135.summary: Students say lectures are engaging and the material fascinating, with weekly readings and several papers. The main complaint is tough grading by readers or GSIs. Reviewers say it is demanding but worth it if you attend, take notes and do the readings.

SOCIOL 139H.summary: Students describe an eye-opening course with a reasonable workload, interesting projects and a caring instructor. Quiz answers come from lectures, so attendance and detailed notes matter, and lowest scores are dropped. One reviewer found grading conversations unpleasant.

SOCIOL 140.summary: Reviewers overwhelmingly praise the lectures as engaging and life changing. Expect heavy and dense reading, though lectures cover much of it, and exams or essays graded fairly but sometimes tough. Take careful notes and attend, since missing lecture means missing a lot.

SOCIOL 141.summary: Students rave about the lectures and the instructor's care, calling the course eye-opening. Readings are dense but manageable, and attendance is taken. Grades rest on a few essays, exams and reading responses, and one reviewer found the essay rubric strict. Office hours and keeping up with readings are recommended.

SOCIOL 149.summary: Reviewers consistently describe engaging, in-depth lectures, a supportive class environment and manageable readings with guides. Exams are essay-style, often take-home and open note. Grades rest on a few assignments, so students advise doing the readings and attending.

SOCIOL 150.summary: Reviewers like the readings but mostly dislike the lectures, calling them repetitive and long. Grading is based on a few papers, reading logs and fieldwork, with no exams in most reports. Opinions split on workload and guidance, with some finding it easy and others finding prompts and expectations unclear.

SOCIOL 160.summary: Students find the content interesting and relevant, and the lectures engaging, with a moderate reading load. The class is writing heavy, and many report tough or inconsistent grading by readers. Slides are sparse, so attending lecture and doing readings is recommended. Instructors are described as accommodating.

SOCIOL 166.summary: Reviewers mostly call it an easy, interesting elective with few assignments, such as essay papers and a multiple choice final. Lectures should be attended since slides are hard to follow alone. Grading on writing can be picky, and one review strongly disliked the teaching.

SOCIOL 167.summary: Reviewers disagree. Many find the topic interesting, the lectures engaging, and the class easy to pass with few assignments. Others complain of inconsistent, nitpicky grading by readers, long regrade processes, and an 8AM time. Since few assignments make up the grade, students say each one matters.

SOCIOL 180C.summary: Reviews are polarized. Many call it an easy A with light workload and interesting content, especially in the online format. Others describe unclear essay instructions, harsh essay grading and an unwelcoming tone. Save the syllabus and grading criteria.

SOCIOL 180I.summary: Reviewers mostly like the course, citing engaging lectures, easy to moderate assignments and quizzes, and fair grading. Attendance is effectively required, with no devices, strict deadlines and papers graded closely to the prompt. A few found the material repetitive.

SOCIOL 182.summary: Students say the content is fascinating and the instructor a leading scholar, but lectures are fast, disorganized and hard to follow. Readings are long, and the grade rests on only a midterm and a final. Detailed notes are essential, though exams are open-note. Reviews are divided between devoted fans and frustrated students.

SOCIOL 189G.summary: Most students describe an interesting, easy class with a light workload and a caring, organized instructor. Exams include questions on specific lecture points, so attending helps. A few reviewers found paper grading unfair or the content one-sided.

SOCIOL 3AC.summary: Reviewers describe an engaging, caring instructor and an easy-to-moderate class. Grades come from a few papers and short quizzes, and lectures cover the readings. Some note reader grading on early essays can be harsh. Students recommend attending lecture and taking good notes.

SOCIOL 5.summary: Students say the material can be dry but lectures are energetic and the course is well organized with clear rubrics. Grades rest on a few research projects, easy low-weight quizzes and a take-home final. Many call it an easy A, though the section instructor strongly affects the experience.

SOCIOL 7.summary: Reviews disagree. Some call it an easy, straightforward stats intro graded on problem sets and two exams. Others find lectures hard to follow, slides unclear, office hours limited and grading harsh. Attendance is described as important.

STAT 133.summary: Reviews split sharply. Older ones call it an easy, manageable R course, while recent ones describe quizzes worth about half the grade that are much harder than homework, with no drops or curve, heavy workload for 3 units, and disorganization. Many recent students would not recommend it.

STAT 134.summary: Reviews are sharply split. Some find lectures clear, grading fair and the class enjoyable, while many describe disorganization, shifting syllabi, tangents, a much harder final and slow grading. Reading the textbook and doing practice problems is the repeated advice, and exams carry heavy weight.

STAT 135.summary: Reviews depend heavily on instructor. Some report disorganization, unclear exam expectations and weak preparation for later courses, while others praise caring, helpful teaching and generous curves. Exams and the final are described as difficult, and many suggest leaning on the textbook.

STAT 154.summary: Few reviews, and they disagree. Several say the machine learning concepts are explained clearly and the structure is organized, while others call it homework heavy with a hard final that does not match the homework or lectures. Grading is described as tough with no curve.

STAT 155.summary: Very few and conflicting reviews. Older ones describe engaging lectures, fair exams, and a caring instructor. Recent ones complain that the course falls behind the material, the instructor seems disengaged, and exams are extremely hard. Experiences seem to vary a lot by semester.

STAT 2.summary: Students say the class is mostly online with recorded lectures, easy to moderate, and good for fulfilling a stats requirement. Homework and quizzes make up much of the grade, and some warn the final or homework volume can hurt. Experiences depend heavily on the GSI, and opinions on lecture quality are mixed.

STAT 20.summary: Students describe a fairly easy, chill class with a lot of coding, where weekly quizzes make up a big part of the grade. Experience depends strongly on the instructor and the GSI. Many praise caring instructors, while some find explanations confusing and grading rubrics unclear.

STAT 33B.summary: Students describe an easy, low-stress 1 unit class that teaches basic R. Assignments and exams are called manageable and graded generously, though some find the homework time consuming for the units and lectures boring. Reviewers say lectures are not essential.

STAT 88.summary: Most reviewers are negative, citing disorganized lectures with off-topic starts, cold calling, slow communication, late exam materials and difficult quizzes. Discussion sections, office hours and the textbook are the repeated advice. A few say the pace is rigorous but fair and the instructor is caring.

STAT W21.summary: Students say this online statistics class is a big time sink, with tedious homework, outdated tools, and inconsistent help. Exams are described as tricky and harder than assignments. Some say the instructor is helpful in office hours and flexible with grading. Reviews lean negative, and self-study is essential.

THEATER 110A.summary: Students rave about this acting class as challenging and rewarding. Feedback is honest and demanding, aimed at preparing actors for the professional world, and the instructor is described as supportive. You must put in real effort to earn a strong grade.

THEATER 110B.summary: Reviewers are extremely positive, calling the instructor caring, clear and transformative for acting skills. Feedback is honest and constructive and can feel intimidating at first. Admission is by audition, and about half get in.

THEATER 111.summary: Students rave about this advanced acting studio, citing constructive, caring feedback and a supportive but demanding environment. Expect at least a few hours of outside work per week and a high bar for preparation. Reviewers say it transformed their acting and recommend it strongly.

THEATER 181.summary: Reviewers are very positive about this production-based class, describing an organized, respectful director who pushes actors while giving creative freedom. Students say it made them better actors and call it a highlight of their year. It is entered through audition.

UGBA 10.summary: Reviews cover several different module instructors and disagree widely. Some modules are called easy, engaging and useful, while others are described as boring, confusing or with unfairly built exams. Common advice is to attend lecture, do the readings, know the formulas, and prepare early.

UGBA 101A.summary: Students report a very demanding course with low exam averages, hard time-pressured exams that differ from practice problems, and little curve. Reviews are mostly negative about lectures and support, with a few saying the instruction is engaging and fair. Expect to study well beyond the lectures.

UGBA 101B.summary: Reviewers are strongly negative, saying lectures are confusing and do not prepare you for exams, which make up about 80% of the grade. Complaints include cold calling, mandatory 8 AM attendance, no practice exams and no makeups. A few say it is manageable with a positive mindset and good studying.

UGBA 102A.summary: Students describe a subject that should be easy but a course they found frustrating. Common complaints are boring or confusing lectures, multiple choice exams that differ from practice exams, and unhelpful support outside class. Many say to rely on the textbook and GSI, or take the course elsewhere.

UGBA 102B.summary: Students say lectures are dry and mostly slide reading, with mandatory participation and attendance, and a heavily weighted cumulative final. Exams are math heavy and can include tricky questions that differ from practice. Some find the instruction funny and fine, but many suggest choosing another section.

UGBA 103.summary: Students call it one of the hardest Haas classes, with low exam means and tests that differ from practice exams. Many say practice exams and slides are key, and exams are open note. Opinions on teaching split between funny and helpful versus confusing, and the section instructor matters.

UGBA 106.summary: Students describe an enjoyable, relevant marketing class built around group projects, presentations and company field trips. Exams are seen as easy with questions largely previewed, making it an easy A. Reviewers advise choosing a good group and attending. A couple note it is light on rigor and less accommodating for DSP students.

UGBA 107.summary: Students say lectures are entertaining and engaging, with cold calling that keeps people alert. The grade rests on a midterm, a final and a research paper, so an A is hard to get even though content is easy. Many complain that writing grading is slow, strict or inconsistent. Some find the humor off-putting.

UGBA 155.summary: Students overwhelmingly call this a meaningful, inspiring class that mixes leadership readings with real-time practice. The workload is readings and reflective work, with easy tests and a generous curve. Participation is central, so it fits quiet students poorly. One reviewer found the content off-topic.

UGBA 175.summary: Students say this law-for-business class is hard, with tough exams that test issue-spotting more than memorization. Lectures are entertaining but come with abrasive humor and cold-calling, so do the reading and come prepared. Most still call it rewarding and a great intro to legal thinking.

UGBA 195A.summary: Students rave about this hands-on entrepreneurship course where you build a real venture. They praise accessible, supportive teaching, useful guest speakers and well-designed assignments tied to startup work. You get out what you put in. One reviewer wanted fewer lecture videos.

UGBA C155.summary: Nearly all reviewers call it an inspiring, reflective and often life-changing class with interesting readings and fairly easy grading. It relies on active participation and a personal, discussion-based format, so quiet students may struggle. One reviewer found it unrelated to leadership.

UGBA C5.summary: Reviews are split. Many call it a rewarding, practical startup class with great guest speakers and a flipped format. Others say the weekly workload is far more than 2 units and that grading and GSI support are poor. There are no exams, only team projects and weekly assignments.

XANTHRO 1.summary: Students say grades come only from two midterms and a final, which are content-heavy and detail-oriented, with no homework. Lectures are funny and full of tangents, and review sessions, extra credit and fossil labs are praised. Opinions on difficulty range from an easy A to very hard.

XGEOG 50AC.summary: Reviewers consistently describe an interesting, well-taught class on California topics such as gentrification, with a caring and accessible instructor. Expect regular readings and attendance, with tests based on lectures and readings. It is considered manageable and a good American Cultures choice.

XMATH 16A.summary: Students say the instructor is very responsive, caring and a lenient grader, with many office hours and recorded lectures. The class is fast, has frequent quizzes and a heavy homework load, and exams make up most of the grade. It can be hard for those new to calculus.

XMATH 1A.summary: Reviews are mixed. Students say the class is hard to follow, theoretical and proof-focused with heavy homework, especially without prior calculus. Others praise accessibility, generous grading and quick returns. Many advise relying on office hours and worksheets, and some suggest taking 1A on campus.

XPHILOS 2.summary: Students rave about the engaging, passionate lectures and approachable instruction. The content and readings can be difficult, and exams are based on readings and lectures, so notes and attendance matter. The final is hard, but many call it one of their favorite classes.

XPHILOS 3.summary: Students find lectures entertaining and engaging, and the instructor accessible and supportive. The material is dense, midterms are difficult with awkwardly worded questions, and grades rely on exams and participation. Reviewers advise attending lecture, participating, and using the slides for studying.

XSTAT 2.summary: Students strongly recommend this introductory statistics class, describing a caring, accommodating instructor who helps even math-averse students pass. Exams and homework are called fair, and office hours and the textbook help a lot. Lectures are sometimes disorganized or confusing.
